name: crt-warp
title: CRT Warp
description: A full-bleed animated background of coarse violet pixels on black, seen through a curved CRT screen with scanlines, glow and grain. It powers on, then flows and bends toward the pointer.
use: A full-bleed backdrop for a retro, synthwave or gaming landing page that wants strong atmosphere.
avoid: The busy high-contrast motion fights any text placed over it, and the always-on shader costs GPU time.
a11y: Reduced motion stops the drift and intro, but the click-to-change pattern has no focusable or keyboard path. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: respected)
looks: The entire stage is a stepped grid of bright violet shapes on black, each edge a square pixel rather than a smooth curve. Fine horizontal scanlines and a soft bloom sit over the blob pattern, with darkened rounded screen edges.
behaves: The picture starts nearly black and brightens as the grid reveals itself, then the plasma shapes keep merging and drifting. Moving the pointer warps the field near the cursor, and a click rolls the screen and switches to a new pattern.
customise: Props set ink and paper colours, speed, variation, level and column counts, curvature, scanlines, mask, bloom and pointer response. Changing the plasma shape needs a shader edit.
weight: heavy: Several full-screen WebGL passes, including a two-direction glow blur, redrawn every frame.
issues: The opening frame is almost pure black, so the effect takes a moment to become visible.
polishWhy: Convincing CRT look with coherent glow, grain and scanlines; coarse pixel steps are intended.
